proceso.titulo: A four-stage process, from definition to production.
proceso.intro: I'm a Design Engineer: I work across design and frontend, and I can take a feature from the moment it's defined to the moment it ships. These are the four stages and what comes out of each one.

etapas.texto: I sit down with product and engineering to work out what needs solving, for whom and under what constraints. Scope and flows come out of that, before I open Figma.
In dense products the problem is rarely visual: it's what gets shown first, what states exist and what happens when something fails. I review what's already there before adding anything new.
I design in Figma with the components and tokens that already exist, and if something's missing I add it to the system. What I hand over can be built without translation.
I take it to React and TypeScript, watching accessibility and performance. Working on both sides lets me adjust the design while building it, instead of defending a file.

proyectos.titulo: A selection of projects across product design, frontend development and visual design.

batuta.texto: Cybersecurity SaaS platform. I work on the frontend, defining experiences in Figma and building them with React and TypeScript. I also build and maintain the design system and develop AI features inside the product.
batuta.nota: These screenshots are of the platform with sample data, so there is no customer information in them. The rest of the product is under NDA.

streetart.texto: Online wine shop with a catalogue, memberships and an admin panel. I handled the visual development, home page, admin dashboard and overall interface consistency.

indice.sitio: Its own system of tokens and components · no CSS framework

streetart.contexto: Online shop for a wine club: authentication, search, combined filters, sorting, memberships, reviews, wishlist, transactional email, user banning and route protection.
streetart.participacion: I handled the visual development: user behaviour analysis, consistency across interface elements, the home page, and the admin profile with its dashboard.

dewey.contexto: App for booking after-school activity slots for kids.
dewey.participacion: I designed the full UX/UI: research, interface components, illustrations, storyboards and wireframes.

cardeuse.contexto: My first professional job as an industrial designer.
cardeuse.participacion: I redesigned every production line and updated the look of fabrics, prints and combinations. I developed new products and brought in manufacturing techniques the factory was not using yet.

nomade.contexto: Degree thesis: a system for moving people in an emergency across sandy terrain.
nomade.participacion: I handled the concept, the development and the working prototype, along with its graphics and its production drawings.

dalle.contexto: A full-stack AI image generator: type a prompt and get an image. Built end-to-end to explore OpenAI's DALL·E model on a modern MERN stack.
dalle.desafio: Wire a deep-learning image model into a responsive web app — handling generation, cloud storage and a clean create flow.
proceso: Built the MERN stack from scratch: Node.js + Express API, MongoDB persistence, React front end
Integrated OpenAI's DALL·E model to generate images from text prompts
Stored generated images on Cloudinary; styled the interface with Tailwind
Split the deployment: backend on Render, frontend on Vercel
dalle.resultado: A working, deployed image generator — try it live.

tms.contexto: A full brand and web redesign for an engineering consultancy — logo, typography and a responsive marketing site in both desktop and mobile formats.
tms.desafio: Refresh the company's identity and ship a fast, smooth site that feels as polished on mobile as on desktop.
proceso: Redesigned the logo, mailing signatures and client presentation into one cohesive identity
Built the responsive site in React + Gatsby, styled with SCSS
Added Locomotive Scroll for smooth, interactive navigation; served media through Cloudinary
tms.resultado: A live, responsive corporate site for TMS Ingeniería.

batuta.contexto: Batuta is a cybersecurity SaaS platform, formerly Metabase Q. As a Design Engineer I own its end-to-end frontend experience: from defining the UX in Figma to shipping accessible, high-performance interfaces in production.
batuta.desafio: Turn complex security workflows into interfaces that are fast, consistent and genuinely usable, while keeping a growing multi-module platform coherent.
proceso: Define requirements, user flows and technical constraints together with product and engineering
Design and maintain a scalable UI / design system in Figma for consistency across the platform
Build high-performance, accessible interfaces in React, TypeScript, Tailwind and Material UI
Drive product discussions and feature prioritization, improving usability across modules
batuta.resultado: Owning both UX and implementation closed design-to-development gaps, standardized components for a more consistent UI, and sped up feature-delivery cycles.
captions: Endpoint posture overview: hardening score, host distribution and vulnerabilities by severity.
Activity log: faceted filters with their counts, date range, and who did what to which object.
Password creation: strength meter and the four rules validating live.
Design system foundations: surfaces, text hierarchy, severity scale and state accents, each token with its usage rule.

sitio.contexto: This site doesn't use a CSS framework. It runs on its own system, using the same principles I apply when working with design systems.
sitio.desafio: A growing product or site faces the same challenge: when every section defines its own colors, spacing and behaviors, consistency starts to break as the system grows.
proceso: Tokens for color, typography, effects and motion.
Reusable components to keep the different sections consistent.
Visual states defined at the system level so their meaning stays consistent.
Shared rules for responsive behavior, instead of solving each section from scratch.
sitio.resultado: Adding a section means reusing the system instead of defining new styles from scratch. The code is public.
